<problem>
For a nonempty finite poset $S$, a linear extension is a total order on its underlying set that extends its partial order. Its order dimension $\dim S$ is the least positive integer $t$ for which there are linear extensions $L_1,\ldots,L_t$ such that $x\le_S y$ if and only if $x\le_{L_i}y$ for every $i$.

For each positive integer $k$, write $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$. Let $\lambda(k)$ be the number of inclusion-maximal intersecting families of subsets of $[k]$: a family $\mathcal F$ is intersecting when $A\cap B\ne\varnothing$ for all $A,B\in\mathcal F$, including $A=B$, and it is inclusion-maximal when no proper larger family of subsets of $[k]$ is intersecting.

Fix an integer $d\ge8$ and put $M_d=\lambda(d-1)+1$. Let $Q_d$ be the poset consisting of all one-element and two-element subsets of $[M_d]$, ordered by inclusion. For a nonempty finite poset $P$, order $P\times Q_d$ by $(p,A)\le(p',A')$ exactly when $p\le_P p'$ and $A\subseteq A'$.

Let $F(d)$ be the supremum of $\dim(P\times Q_d)-\dim P$ as $P$ ranges over all nonempty finite posets with $\dim P\ge3$. Determine $F(d)$ exactly for every integer $d\ge8$.
</problem>

A complete answer to this problem: A complete answer is an exact formula or fully specified rule giving the value of F(d) for every integer d≥8, together with a proof that it equals the stated supremum.

314	### Proof of (18)
315	
316	Remove the bottom two and top two levels of the Boolean lattice, leaving \(N\) vertices. Let \(G\) be their comparability graph.
317	
318	Use a symmetric chain decomposition, randomly permuted by a uniform permutation of the ground set. There are \(w\) chains. For comparable sets of ranks \(a<b\), the probability that they occur in the same chain is
319	\[
320	\frac1{\binom{\max(b,n-a)}{b-a}}.                     \tag{19}
321	\]
322	This follows by counting chains meeting both ranks and using transitivity of the symmetric group on comparable pairs of fixed ranks.
323	
324	For vertices of \(G\), (19) is at most \(1/\alpha\); when the rank difference is at least two, it is at most \(1/\beta\).
325	
326	Let \(U\) be any \(u\)-vertex induced subgraph. If the chains contain \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_w\) members of \(U\), then
327	\[
328	\sum_i\binom{\ell_i}{2}
329	 \ge\frac12(u^2/w-u).
330	\]
331	There are at least \(u-2w\) within-chain pairs whose rank difference is at least two. Another lower bound for their number is
332	\[
333	\frac12(u^2/w-3u),
334	\]
335	obtained by subtracting at most \(u\) consecutive-rank pairs.
336	
337	Taking expectations and then average degrees shows that \(U\) has a vertex of degree at least
338	\[
339	\delta_n(u/w).                                      \tag{20}
340	\]
341	
342	Now count independent sets by branching on such a vertex:
343	\[
344	I(U)=I(U-v)+I(U-N[v]).
345	\]
346	For \(u\le w\), use \(I(U)\le2^u\). For \(u>w\), an inductive upper bound is
347	\[
348	2^w\prod_{j=w+1}^{u}\rho(\delta_n(j/w)).
349	\]
350	To verify the induction, note that these successive factors are nonincreasing, and use
351	\[
352	\rho(t)^{-1}+\rho(t)^{-t-1}=1.
353	\]
354	Taking logarithms and bounding the decreasing right-endpoint sum by its integral gives the parenthesized expression in (18). Finally, allow arbitrary membership on the \(L\) removed vertices, multiplying by at most \(2^L\). ∎

381	\[
382	e^{t\log\rho(t)}(e^{\log\rho(t)}-1)=1

385	\[
386	\log\rho(t)\le W(t)/t.
